security_audit.summary: Most static findings mistake Markdown code spans for Ruby execution or treat fixed Angular CLI commands as unsafe. Dynamic app, prefix, and artifact names remain a medium-risk command-injection concern because the skill does not require validation or argument-safe execution.

remediation.issue: User-derived project, prefix, and artifact names may be interpolated into shell command strings.
remediation.suggestion: Validate names against Angular CLI rules and execute commands with argument arrays or robust shell quoting.

content.value_statement: Starting an Angular project requires many setup decisions and repeated CLI steps. This skill guides consistent scaffolding, generation, builds, AI configuration, and Tailwind setup.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether Angular CLI is available before project creation.
Creates Angular projects with routing, styles, SSR, prefixes, tests, and AI configuration options.
Generates Angular components, services, pipes, directives, interfaces, guards, interceptors, resolvers, enums, and classes.
Runs Angular builds to identify errors before starting the application.
Adds Tailwind CSS through the Angular CLI.
Uses Angular CLI MCP guidance for current Angular best practices.
limitations: Requires Node.js, npm, Angular CLI access, and an internet connection.
Does not define application-specific features, architecture, or visual design.
Does not start the development server without asking the user.
Relies on external package registries and Angular CLI behavior.

use_cases.title: Start a First Angular Project
use_cases.description: Create a structured Angular application with appropriate routing, styles, tests, and initial features.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Scaffolding
use_cases.description: Apply consistent CLI options, naming, AI configuration, and generation practices across new projects.

use_cases.title: Prototype an Angular Product
use_cases.description: Scaffold a buildable Angular prototype with generated services, components, routing, and optional Tailwind CSS.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Angular application named [app name] with routing, SCSS, and tests. Build a simple home page, then verify the build.

prompt_templates.title: Add Generated Features
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Angular application for [purpose]. Generate components for [pages] and services for [data needs], then verify the build.

prompt_templates.title: Configure SSR and Tailwind
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Angular application named [app name] with SSR, routing, Tailwind CSS, and [AI configuration]. Add an accessible responsive shell.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Foundation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a scalable Angular application for [domain]. Define routes, generated artifacts, SSR needs, styling, test coverage, and build verification before implementation.

output_examples.input: Create a customer portal with routing, SCSS, and authentication placeholders.
output_examples.output: A new Angular workspace with routing, SCSS, generated portal pages, authentication services and guards, tests, and a successful build check.

output_examples.input: Build an SSR product catalog and add Tailwind CSS.
output_examples.output: An Angular application configured for server-side rendering, catalog routes, generated data services, Tailwind styling, accessible navigation, and verified compilation.

output_examples.input: Set up a small dashboard without skipping tests.
output_examples.output: A tested Angular dashboard scaffold with generated components, services, routing, selected styles, and build validation before server startup.

best_practices: Confirm project requirements and Angular CLI availability before creating files.
Use Angular CLI generators and track every generated path before extending the code.
Keep tests enabled and run a build before offering to start the application.
anti_patterns: Do not install Angular CLI globally without explicit user approval.
Do not pass unvalidated user text into shell command arguments.
Do not start the development server before implementing features and obtaining user approval.

faq.question: What software does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Node.js, npm, Angular CLI access, and internet access for package installation.

faq.question: Can it create projects with routing?
faq.answer: Yes. It can enable routing during Angular CLI project creation.

faq.question: Does it support server-side rendering?
faq.answer: Yes. It can enable Angular server-side rendering when the project requires it.

faq.question: Can it configure Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: Yes. It adds Tailwind CSS through the Angular CLI and follows Tailwind version 4 guidance.

faq.question: Will it remove generated tests?
faq.answer: No. It skips tests only when the user explicitly requests that option.

faq.question: Does it start the application automatically?
faq.answer: No. It builds features first and asks the user before starting the development server.
